# Selected projects and research

My strongest evidence is research work with traceable publications, complemented by applied Data Science and AI evaluation. Each case study connects a problem, a method, evidence, and the limits of what can be concluded.

<span class="eyebrow">ENVIRONMENT · RESEARCH</span>

## TEB-Veg / TEB-Hydro: urban water processes

Co-author of a peer-reviewed study extending the urban water budget to soil beneath built surfaces, sewer drainage, and within-grid soil-moisture redistribution. The evaluation uses observed sewer discharge from two residential catchments in Nantes and reports performance differences between wet and dry conditions.

[Read the 2018 paper](https://gmd.copernicus.org/articles/11/4175/2018/) · [Read the dedicated research case study](projects/teb-urban-modelling.qmd)
:::
::: {.project-card}


<span class="eyebrow">DATA SCIENCE · AI</span>

## Evaluating hallucination detection for LLM outputs

An industrial benchmark and independent evaluation pipeline comparing factual-consistency approaches using a common protocol, metrics, threshold analysis, and error inspection. The public case study excludes proprietary data, source code, architecture, scores, and rankings.

[Read the case study](projects/llm-hallucination-evaluation.qmd)
:::
:::

## Research publications

::: {.publication-list}
### Reduced-Order Modelling of Dispersion (2008)

**Jean-Marc Brun and Bijan Mohammadi** · Book chapter, *Partial Differential Equations: Modelling and Numerical Simulation*, pp. 245–256.

Reduced-complexity modelling for passive-scalar transport and environmental dispersion, using similarity-based methods rather than solving a full spatial PDE over the entire domain.

[Springer chapter](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5_14) · [Book record](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5)

### Hydrological Evaluation of Urban Greening Scenarios: Application to the City of Nantes, France (2014)

**K. Chancibault, Aude Lemonsu, Jean-Marc Brun, and co-authors** · Conference paper, 13th International Conference on Urban Drainage (ICUD 2014).

This study used the TEB urban scheme with GREENROOF and HYDRO modules to examine hydrological effects of urban greening scenarios in Nantes. It provides an applied example of environmental modelling used to compare planning scenarios; the published abstract describes preliminary results, so this portfolio does not overstate them.

[ResearchGate publication record](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308088054_Hydrological_Evaluation_of_Urban_Greening_Scenarios_Application_to_the_City_of_Nantes_France) · [Bibliographic record from the AGÎLE research team](https://lienss.univ-larochelle.fr/Production-scientifique-de-l-equipe-AGILE)

### Similitude généralisée et modélisation géométrique à complexité réduite (2006)

**Bijan Mohammadi and Jean-Marc Brun** · *Comptes Rendus. Mécanique*, 334(10), 634–638. DOI: 10.1016/j.crme.2006.06.007.

A reduced-complexity approach to passive-scalar transport and dispersion, using similarity solutions in a non-symmetric metric based on transport times and partial observations for model identification.

[Publisher record and abstract](https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/mecanique/articles/10.1016/j.crme.2006.06.007/)

### Contribution mentioned in a public-health exposure report (2006)

**Évaluation de l’exposition aérienne aux pesticides de la population générale — Étude en air extérieur dans quatre sites de l’Hérault en 2006**

The report examines pesticide concentrations in outdoor air at four sites in Hérault and discusses population exposure. Jean-Marc Brun is listed among people who also participated in the study; the report does not specify his individual role or contribution.

[Study report — Santé publique France (PDF)](https://www.santepubliquefrance.fr/sites/default/files/rdd/document/82748_9958-9958-ps.pdf)
:::

## Personal and private work

**Wiki Knowledge** is a personal project in a private repository exploring source ingestion, structured knowledge organisation, validation, and lexical retrieval. The repository is not linked publicly.

## Attribution and evidence

Scientific publications above link to publisher records identifying Jean-Marc Brun as an author. The public-health report is described only as a report that lists him among participants, not as an authored publication. Private industrial work is described only at a level that can be shared publicly; incomplete or unvalidated capabilities are not presented as finished features.
